## NCT07882602
The Effect of Buzzy and VR on Procedure Duration, Pain, Fear, and Parental Anxiety in Children Undergoing Venous Imaging

Intervention: : Vein-imaging device + virtual reality headset group — Patients and families will be informed that the Qualmedi MT-600 Vein-Finder is used to visualize veins; the device will identify the vein for peripheral intravenous catheter (PIVC) insertion. Three minutes before and after the procedure, parents will complete the Descriptive Information Form and State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), and children will complete the Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale and the Children's Fear and Anxiety Scales. The child will be introduced to a white smartphone-compatible "VR BOX 3.0" headset, which will be fitted 60 seconds before the procedure while an Amazon video is played. Disposable covers will be applied to facial-contact areas, and the outer surfaces and screen will be disinfected. Children who wish to remove the headset will be withdrawn. Immediately after the headset is fitted, the nurse will perform catheterization. Primary endpoint: voluntary headset removal; secondary: catheterization success and duration; tertiary: pain, fear, anxiety.
: Vein-imaging device + Buzzy group — Patients and families will be informed that the Qualmedi MT-600 Vein-Finder is used to visualize veins; the device will identify the vein for peripheral intravenous catheter (PIVC) insertion. Buzzy® (MMJ Labs, Atlanta, USA), a reusable device combining cold and high-frequency vibration to reduce procedural pain and distract attention, will be used. Its frozen wing-shaped ice pack is inserted before use and wiped with 70% alcohol afterward. Three minutes before and after the procedure, parents will complete the Descriptive Information Form and STAI, and children the Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale and Children's Fear and Anxiety Scales. Sixty seconds before the procedure, Buzzy will be placed on the antecubital fossa; the nurse will then slide it about 3 cm proximally, apply the tourniquet, and perform catheterization. Primary endpoint: refusal of Buzzy; secondary: success and duration; tertiary: pain, fear, anxiety, and parental anxiety at 3 minutes.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07882602

## NCT07904299
Effect of an Intergenerational Interaction Program Between Older Adults Living in a Nursing Home and Nursing Students on Loneliness, Joy of Life, and Ageism: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Intergenerational Interaction Program — A 6-week intergenerational interaction program in which each older adult living in a nursing home is paired one-to-one with a nursing student. Pairs meet once a week for about 2 hours (1 introductory week + 5 activity weeks). Each session includes welcome and conversation (15 min), joint activity selection (5-10 min), a main activity (60-70 min), and mutual reflection and closing (20-25 min). Activities are chosen jointly by each pair from four categories: games and problem solving, reading and cultural sharing, creative work, and sharing skills and experiences. The program is structured around Allport's contact conditions: equal status, common goals, cooperation, institutional support, sustained contact, and reciprocity. Before the first visit, students receive brief training on aging, communication, and interacting with individuals with cognitive impairment, and they follow defined role boundaries (e.g., no medical or personal care).

## NCT07387770
Assessment of Muscle Deterioration in Hospitalized Cancer Patients Using Surface Electromyography, Dynamometry, and Bioimpedance

Intervention: : Screenig Phase — EMG Parameters Analyzed:

* Amplitude: Root mean square (RMS) during maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) and during sustained contraction, normalized to %MVC.
* Frequency: Median frequency (MDF) and mean frequency (MNF) calculated using the fast Fourier transform (FFT) with 0.5-1 s sliding windows.

Fatigue Indices

* Rate of MDF decline (Hz/s) during sustained contraction.
* Ratio of RMS at the end versus the beginning of the sustained contraction.
* Time to task failure (s) during sustained effort.

Quality Control:

Quality control included real-time visual inspection of signals for movement artifacts, verification of baseline stability (resting activity \<10-20 µV RMS), and complete post-acquisition review with exclusion of segments containing \>20% artifact contamination.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07387770

## NCT07756606
Evaluating the Impacts of Informal Tick and Tickborne Disease Educational Tools on Children

Intervention: : Tick check mannequin — Nymphal and adult blacklegged ticks are glued to the mannequins to mimic potential acquisition or attachment sites. At outreach events, participants are invited to perform a thorough tick check on the mannequin. This activity helps participants identify the different life stages of the blacklegged tick and understand the size differences between nymphal and adult ticks. The "tick check" mannequins also wear both light and dark-colored clothing to show how clothing color affects tick detection.
: Ticks on bagel — Adult and nymphal blacklegged ticks are glued to an "everything" bagel. The bagel is covered in sesame and poppy seeds, which is the comparison commonly used to describe the size of adult and nymphal blacklegged ticks, respectively. Participants are then invited to search the bagel for ticks. The activity demonstrates the size differences between the adult and nymphal life stages and the proper search image for finding nymphs during a tick check.
: LEGO Build-a-Tick — The LEGO tick is an activity that leverages play-based learning to increase awareness of ticks and tick-borne diseases, and it has the potential to significantly enhance our educational efforts by increasing engagement. This Build-a-Tick Kit is comprised of 83 LEGO bricks and offers a hands-on learning experience with multiple learning outcomes. Participants learn about the various morphological parts of a blacklegged tick during the building experience, such as the mouth parts and their function in disease transmission, the number of legs, and the body shapes and colors for an adult blacklegged tick. Additional information on ticks and tick-borne diseases is incorporated into the building instructions included in the Build-a-Tick Kit.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07756606

SUMMARY:

## NCT07918872
Effect of Squatting Position on Birth Outcomes in the Second Stage of Labor in Nulliparous Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial/ Nullipar Kadınlarda Doğumun İkinci Evresinde Çömelme Pozisyonu Uygulamasının Doğum Sonuçlarına Etkisi: Randomize Kontrollü Çalışma

Intervention: : Experimental (Squatting Position) — Until the second stage of labor (until cervical dilation reaches 10 cm), routine clinical care will continue to be provided.

During the second stage of labor, in the active phase when the pregnant woman begins to feel spontaneous urges to push, she will be supported to assume a squatting position on the birthing bed. The woman will adopt the squatting position during uterine contractions and will be allowed to rest in any position she desires on the bed between contractions.

Delivery Phase: After the fetal head crowns, the upper section (head section) of the birthing bed will be elevated to an angle between 45 and 60 degrees. The pregnant woman will lean against the backrest, position her buttocks on the seating area, and place her legs in flexion at the knees, pressing her feet onto the edges of the bed. While the pregnant woman is held in this position, the delivery of the fetus will be performed by Meryem Özdemir, a specialist midwife who is part of the research team.
: Routin Care (Lithotomy Position) — Nulliparous pregnant women included in this control group will receive routine clinical care, and no experimental intervention will be performed until the crowning stage (when the fetal scalp becomes visible at the perineum). For this group, following standard intrapartum protocols, the upper section (head section) of the birthing bed is elevated to an angle of less than 45 degrees during delivery. The pregnant woman is placed in the conventional lithotomy position by positioning her legs on the foot supports attached to the right and left sides of the birthing bed. The deliveries of the pregnant women included in this control group will be conducted in the lithotomy position by the researcher, Expert Midwife Meryem Ozdemir.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07918872

## NCT07920120
Validation of VR Strategies for Knee Osteoarthritis Rehabilitation

Intervention: : Immersive Virtual Reality Walking Conditions — Participants perform repeated walking trials in four immersive virtual reality (VR) environments presented through a head-mounted display (Vive Focus 3): (1) a neutral environment, (2) a safety-promoting environment on low ground, (3) a fear-inducing environment, and (4) a safety-promoting environment on high ground. Each condition involves walking along a straight 6-meter walkway at a self-selected comfortable speed. At least five valid trials are collected per condition whenever feasible, with a minimum of three valid trials accepted if limited by pain, fatigue, or VR discomfort. The environments are designed to manipulate perceived safety and fear during walking.
: Non-VR Walking — Participants perform overground walking without a virtual reality headset along a straight 6-meter walkway at a self-selected comfortable speed. At least five valid walking trials are collected whenever feasible, with a minimum of three valid trials accepted if limited by pain or fatigue. This condition serves as the control for comparison with the four immersive VR walking conditions.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07920120

## NCT06350929
Evaluation of Norepinephrine in the Management of General Anesthesia-Induced Arterial Hypotension in Chronic Heart Failure Patients in the Operating Room.

Intervention: : Cardiac output monitoring by the Starling™ SV Sebac® — During the surgery, the channels and monitoring equipment will be set up according to the usual procedure in the vascular surgery department. As part of the research, the Starling™ SV Sebac® electrodes will be installed (to measure cardiac flow, cardiac index (CI), stroke volume (VES), variations in stroke volume (VVES), and peripheral resistors (TPRI)).

Once the equipment is in place, anesthetic induction will be carried out according to the usual protocol with curarization and mechanical ventilation.

If the appearance of arterial hypotension is noted after anesthetic induction and mechanical ventilation, the patient will be definitively included in the study. As recommended, he will receive norepinephrine to treat hypotension.

The measurements from the monitoring will be collected at 3, 5, and 10 min after the administration of norepinephrine.

10 days after admission to the operating room, hospitalization data will be collected.

## NCT06646991
Comparison of Several Oxygenation Targets With Different Oxygen Interfaces - Impact on Oxygen Flow Rates

Intervention: : Nasal canula - up to 6 liters per minute — Oxygen will be administered via nasal cannula up to 6 liters per minute during this period.

Oxygen flow rates will be adjusted manually, with a gradual increase in flow rates to achieve a oxygen flow rates for reach the peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) target (92% for non chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (non COPD) patient and 90% for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patient).

The steady state will be defined by a fixed oxygen flow rate and a stable SpO2 around the target ±2% for 15 minutes. The average oxygen flow rate during the last five minutes will be used.

Oxygen flow rates will be adjusted manually, with a gradual increase in flow rates to achieve a oxygen flow rates for reach the SpO2 target (92% for non COPD patient and 90% for COPD patient).

The steady state will be defined by a fixed oxygen flow rate and a stable SpO2 around the target ±2% for 15 minutes. The average oxygen flow rate during the last five minutes will be used.
: Open oxygen mask — Oxygen will be administered via an open during this period. Oxygen flow rates will be adjusted manually, with a gradual increase in flow rates to achieve a oxygen flow rates for reach the SpO2 target (92% for non COPD patient and 90% for COPD patient).

The steady state will be defined by a fixed oxygen flow rate and a stable SpO2 around the target ±2% for 15 minutes. The average oxygen flow rate during the last five minutes will be used.
: Simple oxygen face mask — Oxygen will be administered via simple oxygen face mask during this period. Oxygen flow rates will be adjusted manually, with a gradual increase in flow rates to achieve a oxygen flow rates for reach the SpO2 target (92% for non COPD patient and 90% for COPD patient).

## NCT07513662
Feasibility Trial of a Remotely-Delivered Mindfulness-Based Intervention for Adolescents With Migraine

Intervention: : BREATHE with Headache (BREATHE-HA) — BREATHE-HA is a 6-session group mindfulness-based intervention delivered via telehealth for adolescents with migraine. The intervention was adapted from an empirically-supported mindfulness-based intervention for adolescents (Learning to BREATHE; Broderick, 2021). Example activities include breath awareness, body scanning, mindful eating, loving-kindness practice, and mindful movement, as well as activities and discussion focused on improving distress tolerance and enhancing self-care, with examples related to living with migraine.
: Enhanced Standard-of-Care: Headache Education — Enhanced Standard-of-Care is a 6-session group headache education program delivered via telehealth. It will be derived from a manual with fidelity as an attention-matched control in a behavioral trial for pediatric migraine. Headache education will include didactics and discussion on headache symptoms, medication, lifestyle factors for pain management, communication with providers, education on mood/stress, and impact of headaches on school and family.

## NCT07874217
Whole-body Cryotherapy in Those With Chronic Fatigue: A Feasibility Study

Intervention: : Cryotherapy — Intervention: Whole-body cryotherapy intervention consists of 10 sessions administered over 2 consecutive weeks. Sessions will be conducted in an indirect liquid nitrogen-cooled cryochamber with a prechamber set at -60∘°C and a main chamber at -120∘°C. To maximise safety and tolerability in this sensitive patient population, the protocol features a gradual increase in exposure time. Following a 30-second familiarisation session (sessions 1 \& 2), exposure time in the main chamber will increase incrementally from 1 minute on day 1 to a maximum of 3.5 minutes on day 10. Participants will wear standardised protective clothing (gloves, socks, headband, and mask) during all sessions.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07874217

## NCT07894484
Lactium Premedication to Prevent Emergence Agitation: A Dose-Finding Study in Children Undergoing Adenotonsillectomy

Intervention: : Lactium — Lactium solution will be prepared by dissolving each one lentra sachet (150 mg lactium per sachet) in 50 ml of water so that each ml will contain 3 mg of lactium. Oral lactium will be initiated at a dose of 4 mg/kg in the first patient. Dose in subsequent cases will be determined by response to lactium in previous patient using absence or presence of emergence agitation as our primary outcome. A dosing interval of (1 mg/kg) will be used. If the child has no agitation, the subsequent one will receive the same dose with a probability of 0.89 or a reduced dose by 1 mg/kg with a probability of 1/9 (0.11). If the child develops agitation, the subsequent dose will be increased by 1 mg/kg with 100% certainty. If the child responds to the dose of 4 mg/kg, the dose for the next child will remain the same, since this is our minimum dose.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07894484

## NCT07895719
Exercise and Diet Supplements for Older Patients Undergoing TAVI: the IRON-TAVI Trial

Intervention: : Personalized Multidomain Exercise Program — Participants assigned to the multidomain intervention will receive a personalized exercise training program beginning before transcatheter aortic valve implantation and continuing for three months after the procedure. The program includes five supervised exercise sessions, two before and three after the procedure, together with a structured home-based exercise program. Exercise includes walking, mobility exercises, sit-to-stand exercises, balance training, and progressive functional strengthening. Exercise intensity and progression will be individualized according to symptoms, physical performance, clinical condition, and exercise tolerance.
: Oral Protein and Iron Nutritional Supplementation — Participants assigned to the multidomain intervention will receive individualized nutritional counseling and daily oral nutritional supplementation containing protein and iron. Supplementation will start after randomization, before transcatheter aortic valve implantation, and will continue for three months after the procedure. The nutritional intervention will be adapted according to baseline nutritional status, body weight, appetite, renal function, clinical condition, and tolerance. Adherence and tolerability will be monitored throughout the intervention period.
: Usual Care — Participants assigned to the control group will receive standard care according to current clinical practice, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation, guideline-directed medical management, routine follow-up, and general advice regarding physical activity and a balanced diet. No structured study-driven exercise program or protocol-mandated nutritional supplementation will be provided.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07895719

If the concentration is \<350 ng/mL, the dose will be further increased as clinically tolerated. A dose of ≥300 mg/day is not required if the target plasma concentration is achieved at a lower dose. Medication doses will remain stable whenever clinically feasible; changes will be permitted only when clinically necessary for safety or tolerability and will be documented.
: [Phase 2] Magnetic Seizure Therapy (MST) — MST will be administered using a MagPro X100 magnetic stimulator equipped with the MagOption MST module. ## NCT07829107
Comparing the Effectiveness of a Biomarker-plus-clinical Guidelines Algorithm Versus Clinical Guidelines Only for Safely Decreasing Brain Computed Tomography Utilization During Brain Injury Evaluations: The PIONEER Comparative Effectiveness Study

Intervention: : Clinical pathway 1: Guidelines plus biomarkers — Patients will be managed using an algorithm that integrates the Canadian CT Head Rule (CCHR) with i-STAT whole-blood GFAP and UCH-L1 testing. Patients who meet CCHR criteria for CT imaging and those whose CT imaging decision-making is not covered by CCHR (e.g., no loss of consciousness or amnesia) will receive i-STAT testing. Sites will be assigned to one of three implementation waves, with two sites transitioning to the Guidelines + Biomarkers phase every six months. Prior to their assigned transition, sites will continue to use guidelines alone. Once a site transitions to the Guidelines + Biomarkers phase, the integrated biomarker-guided algorithm will become the standard-of-care protocol at that site for eligible patients and will remain the standard of care for the remainder of the study.
: Clinical guidelines only — During the baseline phase, sites will rely solely on established clinical guidelines to guide brain CT utilization in patients with suspected TBI. Specifically, providers will apply the Canadian CT Head Rule, a validated decision instrument that identifies patients at high risk for clinically important brain injury who require CT imaging. All sites will begin in this Guidelines-Only baseline phase and will continue using this approach until their assigned transition to the Guidelines + Biomarkers phase. Sites will transition in three waves, with two sites transitioning every six months.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07829107

A Single-Arm, Dose-Escalation Clinical Study on the Safety of CD19 Sequential CD22 In Vivo CAR-T Cell Immunotherapy for Relapsed/Refractory B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

Intervention: : CD19-Targeted In Vivo CAR-T Injection (first infusion, Day 0); CD22 -Targeted In Vivo CAR-T Injection (second infusion, Day 7) — The investigational products are engineered lentiviral vector-based in vivo gene therapy products. The viral envelope receptor-binding domain has been mutated to abolish native pantropic infectivity, and a targeting module composed of an anti-CD7 nanobody (VHH) and a T/NK-cell-specific ligand (CD58 extracellular domain) has been incorporated into the envelope, enabling specific transduction of circulating T cells and NK cells in situ and expression of a chimeric antigen receptor directed against CD19 (first infusion, Day 0) or CD22 (second infusion, Day 7). No leukapheresis, ex vivo manufacturing, or lymphodepleting conditioning is required. Dose escalation follows a traditional 3+3 design with planned dose levels of 1×10\^9, 3×10\^9, and 6×10\^9 transducing units (TU), guided by the occurrence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs).

## NCT07927465
Neoadjuvant Finotonlimab Plus TP Regimen in Locally Advanced INI-1 (SMARCB1)-Deficient Sinonasal Carcinoma: A Prospective, Multicenter, Single-Arm Phase II Clinical Study

Intervention: : Finotonlimab — Finotonlimab is an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody administered as part of neoadjuvant therapy. It is given intravenously at a fixed dose of 200 mg on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for a total of 2 cycles. It is infused before paclitaxel and cisplatin on the same day. This is the experimental immunotherapy component of the study regimen.
: Paclitaxel — Paclitaxel is a standard cytotoxic chemotherapy agent administered as part of the neoadjuvant TP regimen. It is given by intravenous infusion over 3 hours on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, at a dose of 135-175 mg/m², for a total of 2 cycles. Standard premedication (dexamethasone, diphenhydramine, and cimetidine or an equivalent H2 blocker) is given before infusion to prevent hypersensitivity reactions. Paclitaxel is administered after finotonlimab and before cisplatin.
: Cisplatin — Cisplatin is a standard platinum-based chemotherapy agent administered as part of the neoadjuvant TP regimen. It is given by intravenous infusion at a dose of 70-75 mg/m² on days 1-3 of each 21-day cycle, with the total dose for the cycle divided across the three days, for a total of 2 cycles. It is administered after paclitaxel on day 1. Standard hydration, diuresis, and electrolyte supplementation (potassium and magnesium) are provided. This divided-day schedule is used to reduce acute nephrotoxicity and severe emesis associated with single high-dose cisplatin.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07927465

## NCT07787559
Efficacy of the Epley Versus Semont-plus Maneuver in Patients With Posterior Semicircular Canal Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo: A Randomized Controlled Trial Using Quantitative Video-Nystagmography Measurement

Intervention: : Semont-plus — Semont-plus liberatory maneuver for posterior canal BPPV, performed by a trained therapist at the enrolment visit. From the upright seated position the head is turned 45 degrees toward the nonaffected side. The body is then moved 150 degrees toward the affected side, so that the head comes to lie about 60 degrees below the earth horizontal and the otoconia are carried beyond the vertex of the canal. The body is next moved 240 degrees toward the nonaffected side, which drives the otoconia toward the vestibule, and the participant is finally brought 90 degrees back to the upright position. Each position is held for about one minute or until the induced nystagmus stops. The maneuver is repeated within the same session if positional nystagmus persists. Participants are then taught to perform it on their own at home, as often as they are able, and to record each home session in a diary.
: Epley — Epley maneuver for posterior canal BPPV, performed by a trained therapist at the enrolment visit. From the upright seated position the head is rotated 45 degrees toward the affected ear. The body is then moved backward so that the head hangs below the earth horizontal. The head is rotated 90 degrees toward the nonaffected ear, after which the whole body is rotated downward until the participant faces the floor with the affected ear pointing toward the ceiling. The participant returns to sitting with the head still rotated 45 degrees toward the nonaffected ear, and the head is turned back to neutral at the end. Each position is held until the induced nystagmus stops, and for at least 30 seconds. The maneuver is repeated within the same session if positional nystagmus persists. Participants are then taught to perform it on their own at home, as often as they are able, and to record each home session in a diary.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07787559

Effects of Optokinetic Stimulation Added to Drop Vertical Jump Training on Landing Error Scores and Dynamic Knee Valgus: An Assessor-Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Drop Vertical Jump Training — Following a standardized warm-up and task familiarization, participants will perform two blocks of 10 drop vertical jumps from a 30-cm box toward a target positioned at 50% of their height. After landing on both feet, participants will immediately jump as high and forward as possible and maintain the final landing position for five seconds. Rest periods will be 30 seconds between repetitions and five minutes between blocks. Feedback based on real-time landing error scores will be provided after each block.

Three 60-second exposures will be delivered in each direction before each training block, with 30-60-second rest periods. Active stimulation will total six minutes per block and 12 minutes across the session, excluding rest. The headset will be removed before jump training.

## NCT07822828
A Mechanism Randomised Controlled Trial of a Three-Agent LLM-Augmented mHealth Intervention for Late-Life Loneliness in Older Adults

Intervention: : Hybrid conversational companion application — Companion responses are generated by a large language model through the official DeepSeek API, accessed via Firebase Cloud Functions. The model version is not fixed, so the model identifier returned with each response is logged. Responses are conditioned on the companion's system prompt, conversation history, cross-session memory, and the current input. In reminiscence, the model asks one follow-up question after each answer, and at the end of each week a DeepSeek model drafts a short life-story chapter that a second model checks against the conversation. Four in-app tools (Action Loop, Thought Exercise, Education, Progress). Five LLM-distinctive behaviours are tagged in logs as a cumulative within-arm exposure variable. Conversational text is sent to the model provider; participants are advised not to include identifying information. Participants are encouraged to use the app daily and at least five times per week for four weeks; use is not mandatory and is logged.
: Rule-based conversational companion application — Identical interface, navigation, companion names and personae, tool layer, notification schedule, and in-app assessment prompts. Replies are assembled from pre-written templates by keyword matching and conversational state; no language model is used. In free conversation, Siu Yan's replies are drawn in rotation from a pool of pre-written sentences. The daily check-in is a short conversation with fixed questions, followed by a pre-written response chosen by the participant's answer. In reminiscence, both arms use the same open questions; in this arm each answer is followed by a fixed acknowledgement, and the participant's own answers are arranged, unchanged, into a weekly life-story chapter. No cross-session memory. Conversational content is not sent to any external service; a local safety classifier, hosted by the research team, is used in both arms. Attention- and interface-matched active comparator. Recommended use, expected daily duration, and logging are identical to the experiment
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07822828

## NCT07872384
Improving Functional Recovery in Skilled Nursing Facilities Through Supplemental Mobility

Intervention: : High Intensity Rehabilitation — An 8RM is the dose necessary for most effective strength gains in community-dwelling older adults, and is equivalent to 80% of a one repetition max, which is the maximal load needed to voluntarily complete one repetition of a given exercise with proper form. Activities will include strength training, transfer practice, balance training, advanced ADLs. Clinicians will tailor the intervention for each activity to target overload using 8-repetition maximum for resistance training. Other interventions will be performed to muscle failure or inability to complete the final repetition. Failure is the inability to complete a repetition through the full, available range of motion without significant compensation. Further, high-intensity dosing requires continuous, volitional effort from the patient; therefore, incorporation of motivational interviewing strategies across sessions will maximize patient effort and self-efficacy.
: Safe Transfers and Mobility Program — The Safe Transfers and Mobility Program (STAMP) embeds a mobility aide into daily care. STAMP is a patient-centered, scalable approach to extend the benefits of rehabilitation sessions by increasing mobility throughout the day and reinforcing activity between therapy sessions. Core components are: (1) targeting 45 minutes of additional daily physical activity through support with walking and functional mobility tasks; (2) establishing individualized mobility goals collaboratively set by the therapist and patient, based on functional level; (3) delivering progressive activities with walking distances increased by \~30% weekly, adjusted for patient tolerance; and (4) interdisciplinary coordination to incorporate STAMP sessions into routine care with minimal disruption to clinical workflow. Prior work suggests that 45 minutes of STAMP can at least double daily step counts, and increasing walking distance by 30% per week is feasible even for individuals with low baseline function.
: Usual Care — Usual Care SNFs will continue with routine collection and documentation of physical performance outcomes (gait speed, SPPB, Modified Barthel ADL Index) as standard practice. Importantly, the Usual Care SNF including the facility, rehabilitation clinicians, and patients will not have access to i-STRONGER materials.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07872384

## NCT07927530
Efficacy of Ultrasound-Guided Thoracolumbar Fascia Injection in the Treatment of Chronic Low Back Pain in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized Controlled Trial

Intervention: : Ultrasound-Guided Thoracolumbar Fascia Injection — A single ultrasound-guided thoracolumbar fascia injection will be performed with the patient in the prone position under aseptic conditions. Using an in-plane technique, a 22-gauge needle will be advanced into the middle layer of the thoracolumbar fascia between the quadratus lumborum and erector spinae muscles at the L4 level. Correct needle placement will be confirmed by hydrodissection using approximately 2 mL of local anesthetic. Subsequently, 10 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine and 40 mg of methylprednisolone acetate will be administered into the interfascial plane.
: Standard Conservative Treatment — Standard conservative treatment will consist of structured patient education and a home-based exercise program. The exercise program will include lumbopelvic and core stabilization exercises, abdominal and paraspinal muscle strengthening, hip muscle strengthening, lower extremity stretching, and aerobic activity as tolerated. Participants will receive instructions on correct exercise techniques, maintaining daily activities, and avoiding prolonged bed rest. The program will be recommended for regular home practice throughout the study period.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07927530

## NCT07918599
Comparison of the Effects of Optokinetic Stimulation Added to a Neuromuscular Training Program on Jump-Landing Biomechanics, Visual Dependence, and Reactive Transfer Performance

Intervention: : Neuromuscular Training — Supervised neuromuscular training will be delivered three times per week for six weeks (18 sessions), in addition to usual basketball team training. Each session will last approximately 25-30 minutes and include strength, balance, proximal control, and plyometric exercises. Exercises will progress from bilateral squats, walking lunges, single-leg balance, and drop landings to single-leg squats, drop jumps, single-leg countermovement jumps, and single-leg standing long jumps. Exercises will be performed in 3-4 sets, with 60-90 seconds of rest between sets. Exercise difficulty and repetitions will progress according to the weekly protocol.
: Virtual Reality-Based Optokinetic Stimulation — Optokinetic stimulation will be delivered using a Meta Quest 3S headset and custom Unity software immediately before neuromuscular training, three times per week for six weeks. Participants will track moving balloons with their eyes while keeping their head and trunk as still as possible. Weekly progression will be: week 1, seated, 20 degrees/s, 3 x 30 s; week 2, standing with feet together, 20 degrees/s, 3 x 60 s; week 3, semi-tandem stance, 30 degrees/s, 3 x 90 s; week 4, tandem stance, 40 degrees/s, 3 x 120 s; week 5, tandem stance, 50 degrees/s, 3 x 150 s; week 6, tandem stance, 60 degrees/s, 3 x 180 s. Clockwise and counterclockwise motion will be presented for equal durations. Background rotation speed will be twice the balloon speed. Symptoms will be monitored using the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire, with exposure adjusted according to tolerance.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07918599

Intervention: : Warmth + TENS — A hat device will offer the electrical stimulation (pulse width of 120 milliseconds at about 100 Hz with constant current 0.02mA-0.7 mA, intensity setting at sensory threshold) over 4 acupuncture points over the scalp, including Baihui (GV20), Sishencong (EX-HN1), Fengchi (GB20) and Shenting (GV24). Selection of acupuncture points has been based on the recommendation of traditional Chinese medicine.

Selection of acupuncture points has been based on the recommendation of traditional Chinese medicine.

## NCT03716401
Prognostic Imaging Biomarkers for Diabetic Kidney Disease

Intervention: : MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) — An MRI (or magnetic resonance imaging) scan is a radiology technique that uses magnetism, radio waves, and a computer to produce images of body structures. The MRI scanner is a tube surrounded by a circular magnet.
: US (ultrasound) — An ultrasound scan is a medical test that uses high-frequency sound waves to capture live images from the inside of the body.
: Renal Biopsy — A kidney biopsy involves taking one or more tiny pieces (samples) of the kidney to look at with special microscopes. The microscopes make it possible to see the samples in greater detail.
: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) — Positron emission tomography (PET) uses small amounts of radioactive materials called radiotracers, a special camera and a computer to help evaluate organ and tissue functions. By identifying body changes at the cellular level, PET may detect the early onset of disease before it is evident on other imaging tests.
: Microvascular Assessment — Glycocalyx (a network of membrane proteoglycans and glycoproteins lining all blood vessels) thickness is non-invasively estimated from video clips of sublingual vessels captured using a hand held microscope. Glycocalyx is vital for vascular health; perturbations in the glycocalyx are thought to contribute to numerous vascular health complications including DKD.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03716401

Intervention: : pNGVL4aCRTE6E7L2 — The dose escalation will start from the lowest dose level of 0.3 mg. This dose cohort will consist of 3 participants and a monitoring period of one week after the final dose mandated. If there are 0 participants in the 0.3 dose level cohort that experience dose limiting toxicities (DLT), a new cohort of 3 participants will be vaccinated at the 1.0 mg dose level. If there are 0 participants in the 1.0 mg dose level that experience DLT, then a new cohort of 3 participants will be vaccinated at the 3.0 mg dose level. If there is 1 participant experiencing DLTs, an additional cohort of 3 subjects will be enrolled and treated at the current dose level. If there are 2 or more participants experiencing DLTs in the 3 or additional cohort of 3 vaccinated at the current dose level, then the next lower dose level will be determined as the Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD).

The biological blood test will include the measurement of plasma triglyceride concentrations, total cholesterol and its HDL and LDL fractions, blood glucose, glycated hemoglobin and serum creatinine with estimated glomerular filtration rate according to the CKD-EPI formula. ## NCT04234971
Cost Effectiveness in Alveolar Bone Grafting in Patients With Cleft Lip and Palate: A Randomized Clinical Trial

Intervention: : Intervention group (DBM/BMP) — All patients will undergo a standard procedure for exposure of the cleft alveolar defect and closure of all oronasal fistulae. After induction of general anesthesia, the patient will be intubated with an oral ray tube and prepped and draped in sterile fashion. Pre-operative antibiotics will be given to cover oral flora (i.e. Unasyn or clindamycin if penicillin allergy exists). The intra-oral space will be exposed and the nasal floor and palatal mucosa will be primarily closed to create a water-tight space for the graft. The integrity of the nasal floor mucosa will be tested using methylene blue dye. Following closure of the fistula, the alveolar bone graft will be performed. For the treatment group, 10cc of crushed DBM will be mixed with the micro-sized sponge of rh-BMP-2 (Infuse Bone Graft, Medronic, Minneapolis, MN). The sponge and DBM will then be packed into the defect to completely fill the bony space (FIGURE 3). The anterior mucosa will then be closed.
: Control group(autologous ICBG) — The patient will be induced with anesthesia, prepped, and draped. The intra-oral space will be exposed and the nasal floor and palatal mucosa will be primarily closed to create a water-tight space for the graft. The integrity of the nasal floor mucosa will be tested using methylene blue dye. Following closure of the fistula, the alveolar bone graft will be performed.In the control group, the ICBG will be harvested percutaneously using the Accumed bone graft harvesting system. Briefly, an incision will be made in iliac crest and drill bit inserted. Multiple passes of the drill be used to harvest as much autograft bone as possible from the cancellous region of the iliac crest.Following harvest, fibrin glue will be instilled for hemostasis and a Ropivicaine On-Q pain pump inserted for post-operative pain control. The harvest bone graft will be packed into the alveolar defect in a similar fashion and the mucosa closed anteriorly.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04234971

SUMMARY:

## NCT03055871
Parents and Children Active Together: Examining Motivational, Regulatory, and Habitual Intervention Approaches

Intervention: : Habit formation intervention — In addition to the control content and the planning content, this intervention will include material provided to the family that assists with creating physical activity support habits. The material contains a discussion of what habits are, straightforward examples, planning and pointers for forming habits. A key component of the habit intervention will be planning for context-dependent repetition.
: Physical activity planning intervention — This arm will receive the control education content, but will also be provided with family PA planning material. This material will include skill training content (workbook on how to plan for family PA). The material includes a brainstorming exercise for parents where they list physical activities they think their children have found fun in the past, as well as activities that they would find enjoyable to do as a family. We also have Canadian parental survey data on the most preferred co-physical activities for children 3-6. We will provide this material as prompts/suggestions. This list helps create the template for PA planning by contextualizing what the parents would like to do with their kids.

## NCT04425265
A Randomized Controlled Trial of Plasma Radiofrequency Ablation at Low Temperature Versus Electrocautery Block Resection at High Frequency for Localized Recurrent Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma.

Intervention: : Plasma radiofrequency ablation — Under the guidance of nasal endoscope, the nasopharyngeal tumor and its sufficient safety margin are completely removed through the bilateral nasal cavity. Then investigators use plasma radiofrequency ablation at low temperature to ablate the tumor tissue and normal tissue of the margin along the upper and lower surgical margin until no obvious tumor remained under the naked eye.
: Electrocautery block resection — Under the guidance of nasal endoscope, the nasopharyngeal tumor and its sufficient safety margin are continuously and completely removed through the bilateral nasal cavity. Then investigators separate the posterior part of the nasal cavity and the top wall of the nasopharynx along the bone of the nasopharyngeal fornix, cut the pharyngeal suture, and cut the two sides along the edge of the carina, and then merge along the anterior vertebral muscle surface to the midline incision. Along the the soft palate under the inferior margin, investigators horizontally cut the mucosa of the posterior wall of the nasopharynx, and completely frees the entire soft tissue of the posterior wall of the nasopharynx.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04425265

SUMMARY:

## NCT04364373
D2 vs D3 Lymph Node Dissection for Left Colon Cancer: Multicenter Randomize Control Trial (DILEMMA)

Intervention: : Left colon resection — This procedure is performed for tumours in splenic flexure and proximal and descending colon.

Left colic artery is divided at its origin. Sigmoid arteries and superior rectal arteries are preserved. Inferior mesenteric vein is divided at the lower border of the pancreas. The colon is divided about 10 cm proximal and distal to the tumour. Mesocolic fascia is preserved and the length of the "vessel trunk" of the mesocolon corresponds to the level of lymph node dissection. After removal of the resected colonic segment a handsewn or stapler end-to-end or side-to-side colonic anastomosis is performed.
: Sigmoid colon resection — This procedure is performed for tumours in sigmoid colon. Corresponding sigmoid arteries are divided at their origin. Left colic artery and superior rectal artery are preserved. Inferior mesenteric vein is divide close to the left colic artery. Proximal and distal margin compose 10 cm from the tumour. Mesocolic fascia is preserved and the length of the "vessel trunk" of the mesocolon corresponds to the level of lymph nodes dissection. After removal of the resected colonic segment a handsewn end-to-end or side-to-side or stapler colonic anastomosis is performed.
: Distal sigmoid colon resection or anterior resection — This procedure is performed for tumours in distal sigmoid colon or rectosigmoid junction. Superior rectal artery is divided below the origin of left colic artery. Left colic artery is preserved. Inferior mesenteric vein is divide close to the left colic artery. The colon is divided about 10 cm proximal and 5 cm distal to the tumour. Mesocolic fascia is preserved and the length of the "vessel trunk" of the mesocolon corresponds to the level of lymph node dissection. After removal of the resected colonic segment handsewn or stapler colo-rectal anastomosis is performed.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04364373

SUMMARY:

## NCT04461821
Exhaled Breath Analysis by Secondary Electrospray Ionization - Mass Spectrometry in Children and Adolescents (EBECA)

Intervention: : Real-time SESI-MS breath analysis — Participants will be asked to refrain from eating, drinking, chewing gum use or brushing their teeth at least 1 hour before the measurements will be performed. Room temperature and lighting will be set at the same level for all measurements. Participants will exhale through a disposable mouthpiece into a commercially available SESI source (FIT S.L., Spain). While performing full exhalations, the subjects will keep the pressure through the sampling line at a fixed value monitored by a digital manometer. Breath prints will be collected in real-time recording multiple replicates (typically six in positive and negative ion mode). The whole procedure is absolutely non-invasive and is usually accomplished without any effort in around 15 min per subject.
: Off-line breath analysis — In young children below the age of 4 not capable of completing the on-line exhalation maneuvers, or in cases when the patient needs cannot approach the mass spectrometer, the sample will be collected off-line. They will be asked to exhale into a bag that will be transported to the lab and deflated into the mass spectrometer for analysis. Exhaled breath of patients under anesthesia will also collected using available ventilation system in the operation theatre.
: Blood analysis — Blood analysis done in patients who undergo regular blood sampling needed for clinical routine laboratory controls. This includes i) children and adolescents receiving medications which require TDM ii) patients with acute diseases such as TD1 and pneumonia and iii) patients with chronic diseases such as asthma bronchiale. For those patients where a blood sample is drawn during the clinical routine, an additional blood sample consisting of only several blood drops will be collected using the same blood sampling line. No additional venous puncture for research purpose will be done.
: Saliva analysis — During the diagnostic and therapeutic work-up of T1D patients, saliva samples are collected during the clinical routine. For those patients, additional samples will be obtained by clinically trained investigators.
: Urine analysis — During the diagnostic and therapeutic work-up of T1D patients, urine samples are collected during the clinical routine. For those patients, additional samples will be obtained by clinically trained investigators.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04461821

SUMMARY:

## NCT02604277
Suicidal Behavior in Patients Diagnosed With Bipolar Disorder: The Roles of Biological and Childhood and Adult Environmental Risk Factors

Intervention: : Interpersonal and Social Rhythm Therapy (ISRT) — Interpersonal and Social Rhythm Therapy (ISRT) will be given once a week over a six week period for 55-60 minutes. ISRT emphasizes identifying and maintaining a regular routine in daily life. It includes addressing sleep and solving interpersonal concerns and conflicts by focusing on daily routine.
: Bipolar-Specific Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) — Bipolar-Specific Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) will be given once a week over a six week period for 55-60 minutes.The therapy is directly focused on eliminating or managing specific problems experienced by people with Bipolar Disorder. As part of this intervention, participant's maladaptive thoughts, behaviors and emotions are identified followed by learning how to challenge negative thoughts and reframing into positive, more adaptive thoughts. Additionally, the intervention involves enhancing the participant's coping skills and the ability to view a situation more objectively.
: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) — Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) will be given once a week over a six week period for 55-60 minutes. MBSR is a structured intervention that utilizes mindfulness meditation to reduce suffering associated with physical and psychiatric illnesses. MBSR is nonreligious in nature and aims to encourage an enhanced awareness of moment-to-moment experience of noticeable mental processes.
: Psycho-education & Understanding Bipolar Medications Therapy — Psycho-education \& Understanding Bipolar Medications Therapy will be given once a week over a six week period for 55-60 minutes. Psycho-education \& Understanding Bipolar Medications Therapy aims to provide psycho-education about Bipolar Depression as well as provide a platform for participants to address concerns about managing their illness. Issues such as managing symptoms, reducing relapses and hospitalizations as well as maintaining gains will be discussed
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02604277

SUMMARY:

A bone marrow biopsy removes bone with the marrow inside and is done prior to the aspirate. Each biopsy and aspirate procedure takes approximately 15 minutes total. ## NCT04363983
Interaction Between Host, Microenvironment and Immunity on Gastrointestinal Neoplasms: A Retro-prospective Cohort Study

Intervention: : Blood sampling — Blood collection (50 ml) will be performed for all patients at baseline, at 1 month post-operative for resected patients (+ at the end of neoadjuvant treatment / before surgery if patient receives neoadjuvant treatment), and at 2-3 months after the beginning of the treatments in patients with metastases (+ at each progression).

Following analysis should be performed with

* serum for protein assays and characterization analysis of cytokines, new tumor markers and micro-RNA ...;
* plasma for protein assays and characterization analysis of micro-RNA, VEC (the content of proteins, RNA, micro-RNA and DNA) and metabolomics;
* PBMC for flow cytometry analysis, isolation macrophages;
* whole blood for circulating tumor DNA (mutations by NGS, ddPCR,…; methylation) and circulating tumor cells.
: Liver biopsy — An intraoperative liver biopsy will be performed at free edge of liver with a triangular sample for local resected patients.

This biopsy will be done with scissors, then patients will receive intraoperative hemostasis with mono- or bipolar coagulation. This procedure will be under laparoscopy or laparotomy without extending standard processing time.

This biopsy seeks to allow the evaluate liver modifications testifying the preparing for premetastatic niche, which would allow to identify the patients with risk for hepatic relapsing; the same analysis on the tumors will be performed.
: Stool collect — Stool collection will be performed for all patients at baseline, at 1 month post-operative for resected patients (+ at the end of neoadjuvant treatment / before surgery if patient receives neoadjuvant treatment), and at 2-3 months after the beginning of the treatments in patients with metastases (+ at each progression).

Analysis will be performed for microbiota and metabolism analysis.
Link: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04363983

SUMMARY:
